title: Case study: notification service

kcs.statement: A notification service accepts requests, checks user preferences and rate limits, and puts each message on a separate queue per channel (push, SMS, email). One slow provider then cannot block the others.
Channel workers retry provider failures with exponential backoff and move exhausted messages to a dead-letter queue. An idempotency key per notification stops retries from sending duplicates.
Templates are rendered at send time from stored templates and user locale. Bulk campaigns are throttled to protect providers' rate limits and transactional notifications.

problem_ideas: The SMS provider is down for 20 minutes. Trace what happens to push and email notifications.
A worker sends an email and crashes before the ack. Explain how duplicates are prevented.
A marketing blast of 50M emails collides with password-reset emails. Design priority handling.
Estimate the queue depth if the email provider accepts 1,000/s and the campaign enqueues 10,000/s.
Store user opt-out preferences and check them without a database read per message.
Design delivery status tracking (sent, delivered, opened) for analytics.
